column47: The Biochemistry, Molecular and Structural Biology (BMSB) Graduate Program is designed for students who want to conduct research at the interface of chemistry, biology and medicine. Our primary goal is to train the next generation of scientists to be leaders in academia, biotechnology and the pharmaceutical industry. The core of the program is the research experience, where students work in the laboratories of world-renowned faculty to make original and impactful discoveries. Students choose a research advisor from among over 40 faculty members in the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry. These faculty members have research interests that span the entire range of biochemistry and molecular biology, including structural biology, proteomics, genomics, epigenetics, metabolism, and bioenergetics. The research is often interdisciplinary, involving collaborations with other departments such as microbiology, immunology and molecular genetics; biological chemistry; medicine; and physics. Our faculty are also members of many interdisciplinary research centers and institutes at UCLA, including the Molecular Biology Institute (MBI), the California NanoSystems Institute (CNSI), the Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center, and the Eli and Edythe Broad Center of Regenerative Medicine and Stem Cell Research.

column47: The UCLA Graduate Certificate in Digital Humanities is designed for students who are currently enrolled in a graduate program at UCLA. column47: The Graduate Certificate in Early Modern Studies is designed to allow students to develop a program of study that transcends traditional departmental and disciplinary boundaries. column47: Experimental Critical Theory (ECT) is an interdisciplinary program and graduate certificate at UCLA that offers a sustained venue for students to integrate the study of critical theory with their work in their home departments. ECT is a laboratory for experimenting with theoretical methods and their potential to push the limits of disciplinary boundaries and generate new modes of thinking. The program brings together faculty and graduate students from across the university to explore the intersections of philosophy, literature, social theory, and the arts.

column38: UCLA Fielding School of Public Health
column47: The Graduate Certificate in Food Studies is designed to provide UCLA graduate students with a multidisciplinary perspective on the impact of food on people and the planet. The 12-to-20-unit certificate program, based at UCLA Fielding but open to any UCLA graduate student, provides a common ground for students from a wide range of disciplines to come together and think critically about food’s impact on people and the planet. It allows students to engage with their peers from around the campus to learn how their specific field can contribute to addressing food-related issues, as well as how other fields are approaching them. The core courses examine food from both the perspective of human health and the environmental impact. In addition to the core courses, students choose elective courses from a wide range of fields, which can include public health, medicine, management, law, history, geography, anthropology, public policy, urban planning, and environment and sustainability.

column16: The Urban Humanities Certificate is open to all currently enrolled UCLA graduate students (Masters and PhD) in any department. To apply, students must submit a CV/resume, a 1-page statement of interest, and a brief writing or portfolio sample (5-10 pages or equivalent).

column47: UCLA’s Urban Humanities Initiative (UHI) is a program of research and study that brings together the humanities, architecture and urban design, and urban planning. Funded by the Andrew W. column47: The Graduate Certificate in Writing Pedagogy provides a structured environment for UCLA graduate students to develop a specialization in the theory and practice of teaching writing at the college level. The program is designed to integrate pedagogical development with students’ ongoing graduate coursework and research, emphasizing the connection between writing, learning, and disciplinary knowledge. To earn the certificate, students must complete the following requirements: 1. Two courses in writing pedagogy: Students must take English 495A (Pedagogy of Writing) or an equivalent departmental course in the pedagogy of writing. They must also take one additional 4-unit course on writing pedagogy. 2. Teaching experience: Students must have at least two quarters of experience teaching writing-intensive courses at UCLA. 3. Pedagogy workshops: Students must participate in at least two pedagogy workshops offered by Writing Programs or other campus units. 4. Teaching Portfolio: Students must submit a portfolio that includes a statement of teaching philosophy, sample syllabi, and other evidence of teaching effectiveness.

column38: UCLA Fielding School of Public Health
column47: The Global Health Certificate is an interdisciplinary program for graduate students at UCLA. The program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the major issues in global health and to equip them with the knowledge and skills necessary to address these challenges. The certificate is open to all UCLA graduate and professional students.

column2: Bixby Population and Reproductive Health Certificate
column16: The Bixby Certificate Program is open to UCLA graduate students who are currently enrolled in any of the university’s degree programs. Students must be in good academic standing. The application for the Bixby Certificate Program consists of contact information, current degree program, and two short-answer questions (no more than 250 words each) describing interest in the field of population and reproductive health and how the Bixby Certificate would benefit career goals. Applicants must also submit a current resume or CV. Letters of recommendation and GRE scores are NOT required.
column47: The Bixby Certificate in Population and Reproductive Health provides UCLA Fielding School of Public Health students with a deeper understanding of the factors that influence the health of populations, with a focus on reproductive health and rights. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in reproductive health, family planning, and population dynamics, both domestically and internationally. Students gain skills in demographic methods, program evaluation, and policy analysis. To receive the Bixby Certificate, students must complete: a minimum of 16 units of coursework in population and reproductive health; a 400-hour field experience in a population or reproductive health-related organization; and a culminating project (e.g., master’s report, thesis, or dissertation) on a population or reproductive health topic.

column47: The Leaders in Sustainability (LiS) graduate certificate program is designed for UCLA graduate students (masters and doctoral) who want to add a sustainability lens to their primary field of study.
